report:
Reviewed the complete claim, single ordinary implementation association in sage_ir::parse, and sole TODO test sage_meta::todo::modules_parse_dependencies. The permitted dependency set is module source, scope, edition, and generated parse source; resolved names, checked interfaces, other items' bodies, and trait results are forbidden. In the captured parse/mod.rs, parse_str_to_cst builds Parser from db/source/scope/text, tree_sitter_parse consumes text, and parse_item_list dispatches syntax nodes and constructs source spans. These entry-point observations support the intended separation; they do not establish a complete transitive query dependency trace, cache behavior, or edition handling, and I do not claim that proof from the dispatcher alone.

The complete associated test is an empty TODO body, with no behavioral assertions. Its explicit matrix defers cold traces restricted to permitted inputs, unchanged warm requests doing no parse work, and reuse after changes to semantic facts that leave parse inputs unchanged. That matrix accounts for the forbidden semantic categories as well as allowed-input separation. Completion requires trace-observable parse/query execution and fixtures that vary resolved names, interfaces, unrelated item bodies and trait results independently of source/scope/edition/generated source. A semantic lookup accidentally added below dispatch would not be detected by this placeholder; such transitive verification remains explicitly deferred. The existing TODO is a justified disclosure of this verification gap, not passing behavior or complete implementation evidence. No N/A or additional test entries exist. No additional edits are required to this deferred accounting.

Baseline: independently compared both historical whole-file snapshots to current files byte-for-byte; parse/mod.rs and semantic_spec.rs exactly match. Reassessed the supplied historical rationale against current claim and evidence rather than treating its decision as approval. Source assessment used current captured fragments plus the recorded review specification; no historical helper contents were used. Execution: personally ran review start, review read, and snapshot comparison, then review record. No behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. Coordinator-reported 321 sage-meta tests and cargo build success are separate execution evidence and do not establish this deferred claim.
